headline: The dollar has pushed the euro down to a two-month low.
summary: Coming into September, many traders still expected the Fed to eventually cut rates, but instead the Fed raised its key rate by 0.25% to 3.75-4.00% on September 16 — its first hike since 2023 — citing persistent inflation. Since then, strong US business activity data and hawkish comments from Fed officials have pushed the odds of another Fed hike in October up to roughly 65-70%, even though the ECB also raised its own rate by 0.25% and eurozone business activity hit a multi-year high. Despite the ECB move, the euro has actually weakened against the dollar, dropping to around $1.14 — its lowest level in about two months — as US bond yields climbed to their highest since 2007.

whatMattersNext.label: US September jobs report and eurozone flash inflation estimate

forYou: If you're converting USD to EUR right now, you'll get a bit fewer euros per dollar... wait, actually a bit more dollars go further since the euro is weaker, so your USD paycheck stretches slightly more in euro terms than it did a month ago.
